key_insight: A sharp-crack deep energy method can jointly solve transient thermo-mechanics and crack growth without phase-field regularization by embedding the crack directly into the neural inputs.
engineering_relevance: This provides a mesh-free surrogate framework for predicting thermally driven crack initiation and propagation in brittle or graded structures under coupled loading.
method: Two neural networks approximate temperature and displacement on a cracked domain.
A scalar crack embedding plus Williams-tip enrichment lets fields jump across the crack and capture tip singularity.
Training minimizes staggered conduction and thermoelastic energy with Monte Carlo sampling refined near the crack tip.
evidence_signal: The method matches a published thermal stress-intensity factor within 0.11% and reproduces crack initiation/paths on benchmark cases under mechanical, thermal, and combined loading.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on careful crack-tip sampling, contour-radius checks for stress-intensity extraction, and a stable staggered training setup.
paper_title: An extended deep energy method for thermo-mechanical crack propagation
